newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares stretch losses, Telebras plummets.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares stretch losses, Telebras plummets.

text.p: Brazil stocks extended losses, plummeting 6.02 percent in moderate turnover, with Telebras preferred plunging 5.38 percent to 149.50 reais, surprising traders and equity analysts.
"It's difficult to say anything right now. Everybody wants to leave through the same door, that's why the market is plunging," said John Carioba, from Indusval brokerage.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active stocks was 765 points lower at 11,933 points. Turnover was a moderate at 490.8 million reais ($454.4 million).
Carioba said speculative trades are driving the market lower. However, he said the bolsa is expected to reach levels that will bring investors back to the buy side.
"But when the rebound will begin, it's hard to say," he said.
He also noted that local equity funds, which in June contributed to pushing share prices higher and boosting volume, were on the sidelines.
Others, however, believe those funds are participants in today's blood-letting.
Speculation was triggered by concerns related to currency devaluations in some Asian countries and their eventual impact on the Brazilian economy.
Alvaro Bandeira, director at Senso brokerage house, said that to compare Brazil with those Asian countries makes no sense.
"Any comparison is economically baseless," he said.
Brazil shares some of the aspects that made those Asian nations vulnerable to speculative attacks on their currencies -- a large current account gap and overvalued currency.
But Brazil also has $57 billion in reserves to ward off any speculative attack on the real currency, analysts said.
